# How to turn a meeting into clear notes and action items with AI

**Imagine never having to stress about taking minutes during a busy work call again.** By the end of this guide, you will know how to use an AI assistant to turn a chaotic wall of text or scribbled notes into clean, structured action items for your team.

## Before you start
- **An account** with a free AI assistant (such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini).
- **Some rough text** from a recent meeting. This could be a transcript (a word-for-word written record of everything spoken, automatically generated by video call software like Zoom or Teams) or just your own messy typed notes.
- **Privacy awareness**: Ensure you do not upload highly sensitive corporate secrets or personal customer details into free, public AI tools. 

---

## Step 1 — Gather and clean your meeting text
Before feeding anything to an AI, gather your raw notes or copy the transcript from your video conferencing app. Take a quick look through the text and delete any highly private information—like bank account numbers or specific client passwords.

---

## Step 2 — Open your AI assistant
Open your preferred web browser and go to your chosen AI tool. Think of these tools as friendly, highly capable office assistants who are ready to read and write at your command.

---

## Step 3 — Write your prompt (instruction)
To get the best result, you need to write a clear **prompt** (the specific instruction or question you type into an AI tool to tell it what to do). 

For a great meeting summary, you want to tell the AI exactly who it is representing, what to look for, and how to format the output. Copy and paste the template below into the chat box.

💬 **Example prompt:**
> "Act as a professional administrative assistant. Below is a raw meeting transcript. Please organise this text into three distinct sections:
> 1. **Summary:** A three-sentence overview of the main topics discussed.
> 2. **Key Decisions:** A bulleted list of any final decisions made during the call.
> 3. **Action Items:** A list of tasks, clearly showing who is responsible for each task and the deadline (if mentioned).
> Keep the tone professional, clear, and direct."

---

## Step 4 — Paste your text and press send
Right below your prompt, paste your messy notes or transcript. If the text is very long, don't worry. Most modern AI systems have a large **context window** (which is simply the AI's short-term memory—the maximum amount of text it can read and remember in a single go). 

Press the send button (usually shaped like a small paper plane or arrow next to the text box) and watch the AI organise your notes in seconds.

---

## Step 5 — Refine the results
If the first draft isn't perfect, you can easily ask for changes. You do not need to start over; just talk to the AI like a human colleague.

💬 **Example follow-up prompts:**
- *"Can you make the action items list shorter and focus only on Dave's tasks?"*
- *"Reword the summary so it sounds a bit more casual, ready to put into our team Slack channel."*

---

## Common mistakes
- **Trusting the AI blindly:** AI tools can sometimes **hallucinate** (a term for when the AI confidently makes up facts, names, or dates that were never actually mentioned). Always read through the output once to verify accuracy before sharing it.
- **Uploading client details:** Unless your business has a secure, private enterprise agreement with the AI provider, avoid pasting private customer names or company financials. Swap real names for placeholders like "Client A" if you want to be completely safe.
- **Vague instructions:** If you simply ask the AI to "summarise this," you might get a long, rambling paragraph. Always ask for specific bullet points and structures to save yourself editing time.

---

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** You can use this exact method to organise messy family group chats about upcoming holidays, sorting who is bringing what into a neat checklist.
- **For your business or work:** You can stay 100% focused on the human conversation during a meeting, knowing you do not have to scribble everything down frantically.
- **If you're just getting started:** This is the ultimate low-risk way to experience how AI can save you hours of administrative work every single week.

---

## Try it now
Open an AI tool right now, copy the simple text below, and paste it into the chat to see how easily it works.

**Copy this text:**
> "Please turn this messy note into a neat bulleted list of action items: 'Dave needs to call the plumber by Wednesday morning. Sarah is going to check the budget tomorrow. We decided to reschedule the team lunch to next Friday.'"
